sections.html:
Walworth County splits collection by season. Your town, village or city treasurer handles the first payment. The county treasurer handles July and anything late. The county office is in the Government Center, 100 W Walworth Street, Room 103, Elkhorn, WI 53121. Call 262-741-4251; the counter is staffed 8 am to 4:30 pm on weekdays.

Municipalities mail their bills by mid-December. If nothing has come by December 20, phone your local treasurer. An unreceived bill is no excuse for a late payment, and interest still builds.

sections.h2: Due dates and where to pay
sections.html:
Pay in full on or before January 31 at the local municipality, or split the bill and send the second half to the county by July 31. A total under $100 is due all at once in January.

SituationDeadlinePay to
Full paymentJanuary 31Local municipality
First installmentJanuary 31Local municipality
Second installmentJuly 31Walworth County Treasurer
Tax bill under $100January 31, all at onceLocal municipality
Anything paid after February 1As soon as possibleWalworth County Treasurer

See the county's Pay Taxes page for the same schedule. Skip the first installment and the full unpaid balance turns delinquent as of February 1. Wis. Stat. 74.11 gives five working days after January 31 for a payment to be received, but do not count on that cushion.

sections.h2: Ways to pay the county treasurer
sections.html:
Options are the counter, the mail, a drop box and the web. The drop box stands at the west end of the median in the north parking lot, near the Elkhorn Police Station. Web payments go through the county's Ascent Land Records site, which is open around the clock.

Convenience fees:

  • Credit card: 2.29 percent per transaction, $2.00 minimum
  • Debit card: 1.5 percent per transaction, $2.00 minimum
  • E-check: $1.00 per transaction

During December and January the county treasurer does not process real estate payments, so everything in that window goes to the municipality where the parcel sits. When you mail a check, enclose the bill stub or write the parcel number on it. A stamped, self-addressed envelope gets you a receipt, though the receipt is not valid until the payment clears the bank. A copy of a bill costs $1. Send a self-addressed stamped envelope, the tax year and the tax key number to P.O. Box 1001, Elkhorn, WI 53121.

A delinquent balance gains 1 percent interest and a 0.5 percent penalty each month from February 1, and a partial month is billed as a whole one. That is 1.5 percent monthly on the unpaid tax, and the county treasurer receives these payments.

A parcel that stays delinquent for two or more years can be foreclosed. The county follows the in rem tax foreclosure procedure, supervised by its treasurer. Wis. Stat. 75.521 lets the treasurer file a list of liens with the circuit court two years after the tax certificate date. Anyone with an interest in a listed parcel can redeem by paying the listed sums, interest and the county's costs, or can file a verified answer within 30 days after the last redemption date in the published notice. If nobody redeems or answers, the court enters judgment vesting the property in the county.

If you want to sell while behind, ask the treasurer for a payoff figure early. Costs grow as the case moves forward, and a clear payoff number lets your closing agent pay the county out of your proceeds.

sections.h2: How do I challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Your local assessor is the first call, since the county treasurer passes all valuation questions down to the municipality. If the assessor cannot fix it, your municipal board of review is the next stop.

Under Wis. Stat. 70.47 that board sits once a year in a 45-day window opening the fourth Monday of April. Its rules in brief:

  • Tell the board, in writing or by voice, at least 48 hours before the first meeting that you intend to object.
  • Hand in a written objection during the first two hours of that meeting.
  • Bring proof. The assessor's number is presumed right until you rebut it.

There is no way around the board. A claim for an excessive assessment under Wis. Stat. 74.37 must be served on the municipal clerk by January 31 of the year the tax is payable, and only after you went through the board and paid on time. The municipality then has 90 days to respond. If it says no, you have 90 days from the notice to sue in circuit court.

Two state credits can appear on a Walworth County bill. The lottery and gaming credit goes to owners whose primary residence was the home on January 1 of the levy year. The First Dollar Credit applies to state taxable parcels with a real property improvement and has done so since the 2008 tax bill.

The Wisconsin Department of Revenue has the details on both. If a credit you expect is not on your bill, ask the county treasurer or your local treasurer how to apply.

Walworth County runs along the Illinois border, with Elkhorn as the county seat. In 2020 it had 106,478 residents and 53,146 housing units, 20.3 percent of them vacant, and 31.1 percent of occupied homes were rented. Tourism around Lake Geneva keeps the second-home and vacation market busy.

Several municipalities straddle county lines. Burlington sits mostly in Racine County, Whitewater partly in Jefferson County, Genoa City partly in Kenosha County and Mukwonago mostly in Waukesha County. Look at the county named on your tax bill before deciding which treasurer to phone.

Before a cash sale closes, ask the closing agent to request a current tax statement from the treasurer so any balance for the year is settled at the table. Know which installments you already paid, and to whom, since the January payment went to the municipality and the July payment goes to the county.

faqs.q: When are Walworth County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The full tax or first installment is due January 31, and the second installment is due July 31. A bill under $100 is due in full by January 31. First payments go to the local municipality and second payments to the Walworth County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Where is the Walworth County Treasurer's office?
faqs.a: In the Government Center at 100 W Walworth Street, Room 103, Elkhorn, WI 53121, phone 262-741-4251. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1001, Elkhorn, WI 53121, and the counter is open 8 am to 4:30 pm Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How much interest is charged on late taxes?
faqs.a: Interest of 1 percent plus a 0.5 percent penalty accrues monthly, 1.5 percent in total. It starts February 1, and a partial month counts as a whole one.

faqs.q: Can the county foreclose on unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. A parcel that stays delinquent for two or more years can be foreclosed through the in rem procedure. Interested parties can redeem by paying what is owed plus costs before the redemption date in the published notice.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about my assessment?
faqs.a: Start with your local assessor, then go to your municipal board of review. The county treasurer does not set or change assessed values.
